hooks.name: useBoolean
hooks.summary: Boolean state with toggle helpers.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for panels, switches, and any on/off UI.
hooks.description: You have a panel, switch, or “show more” control. Pass true or false as the starting value. You get named helpers to turn it on, turn it off, or flip it — without a raw boolean plus setState(!value) in three places.

api.explanation: Keeps a boolean in React state and returns helpers so you can flip, force on, or force off without writing setState yourself.

arguments.name: initialValue
arguments.description: Required starting value: true or false.

returns.description: The current flag plus stable callbacks to change it.

fields.name: value
fields.description: Whether the flag is currently on.

fields.name: toggle
fields.description: Flips value from true to false or the reverse.

fields.name: setTrue
fields.description: Sets value to true.

fields.name: setFalse
fields.description: Sets value to false.

fields.name: setValue
fields.description: Escape hatch for any boolean update, including functional updates.

hooks.name: useDisclosure
hooks.summary: Open, close, and toggle for menus and dialogs.
hooks.whenToUse: Use when UI has an explicit open/closed lifecycle.
hooks.description: A menu, drawer, or dialog is either visible or not. Buttons need Open, Close, and sometimes Toggle. useDisclosure is that lifecycle so you are not mixing a boolean named isOpen with ad-hoc setters.

api.explanation: Named open/close/toggle helpers for UI that has a visible and hidden state, such as menus, drawers, and dialogs.

arguments.name: initialOpen
arguments.description: Whether the surface starts visible.

returns.description: Visibility flag and the three actions you typically wire to buttons.

fields.name: isOpen
fields.description: True while the surface should be shown.

fields.name: open
fields.description: Shows the surface.

fields.name: close
fields.description: Hides the surface.

fields.name: toggle
fields.description: Flips isOpen.

hooks.name: useDebounce
hooks.summary: Delay updates until the value stops changing.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for search inputs and expensive derived work.
hooks.description: The user is typing into search or a filter. You do not want to hit the server or filter a huge list on every keystroke. Debounce the value, then use the lagged copy for the expensive work. The input itself stays instant.

api.explanation: Returns a copy of value that only updates after value has stayed still for delayMs. The first render returns the original value immediately.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The rapidly changing source, such as an input string.

arguments.name: delayMs
arguments.description: Idle time in milliseconds before the returned value catches up.

returns.description: The lagged value. Use this for search queries, filters, or expensive work.

hooks.name: useThrottle
hooks.summary: Limit how often a value updates.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for scroll, resize, and rapid input where you still want periodic updates.
hooks.description: A value changes often — scroll position, pointer coords, or rapid typing — and you need updates at a steady cadence rather than waiting for silence. Throttle keeps the first update in a window and a trailing latest value.

api.explanation: Returns a copy of value that updates at most once per delayMs. The first change in a window applies immediately; a trailing update keeps the latest value.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The rapidly changing source, such as scroll position or input text.

arguments.name: delayMs
arguments.description: Minimum milliseconds between updates.

returns.description: The throttled value. Prefer this over debounce when you need periodic updates while typing or scrolling.

hooks.name: useInterval
hooks.summary: Declarative setInterval that always calls the latest callback.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for polling and timers. Pass null to pause.
hooks.description: You need a ticking clock, a poll, or a progress bar that advances on a schedule. You are tired of setInterval inside useEffect, stale closures, and forgetting clearInterval. Pass null to pause without tearing the component down.

api.signature: useInterval(callback: () => void, delayMs: number | null): void
api.explanation: Runs callback on a timer, always calling the latest function without resetting the interval. This is a side-effect hook: it does not return a value.

arguments.name: callback
arguments.description: Work to run each tick. You can change this every render; the interval still keeps its schedule.

arguments.name: delayMs
arguments.description: Milliseconds between ticks. Pass null to pause; passing a number again resumes.

returns.description: Nothing. Drive UI from your own state that the callback updates.

caveats: Clearing happens automatically when the component unmounts or delayMs changes.

hooks.name: useCopyToClipboard
hooks.summary: Copy text with the Clipboard API.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for share and copy buttons.
hooks.description: A “Copy invite link” or “Copy code” button. You need to write to the clipboard and show Copied for a moment. This hook is that interaction, including failure when the browser blocks clipboard access.

api.explanation: Wraps navigator.clipboard.writeText and remembers the last string that copied successfully so you can show a “Copied” label.

returns.description: Clipboard helpers plus the last successful payload.

fields.name: copiedText
fields.description: Last text that copied, or null if none / last copy failed.

fields.name: copy
fields.description: Writes text. Resolves true on success, false if the API is missing or the write fails.

fields.name: reset
fields.description: Clears copiedText back to null.

caveats: Requires a secure context (HTTPS or localhost) for the Clipboard API.

hooks.name: useLocalStorage
hooks.summary: Persist JSON-serializable state in localStorage.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for user preferences that should survive refresh.
hooks.description: A preference should survive refresh: theme, sidebar width, last used project. You want useState that writes JSON to localStorage. This is that pair of value and setter, with a fallback if storage is empty or corrupt.

api.explanation: Same idea as useState, but the value is JSON-serialized into localStorage under key so it survives refresh.

arguments.name: key
arguments.description: localStorage key. Changing it re-reads that entry.

arguments.name: initialValue
arguments.description: Used when the key is missing or stored JSON cannot be parsed.

returns.description: A state tuple. setValue accepts a value or a function of the previous value, like useState.

fields.name: value
fields.description: Current parsed value.

fields.name: setValue
fields.description: Writes to React state and localStorage.

caveats: Values must be JSON-serializable.
Corrupt JSON in storage falls back to initialValue.
Write failures (quota, private mode) are ignored; state still updates in memory.

hooks.name: useSessionStorage
hooks.summary: Persist JSON-serializable state in sessionStorage.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for drafts that should survive refresh but clear with the tab.
hooks.description: A draft or wizard step should survive refresh but not outlive the tab. Same shape as useLocalStorage, backed by sessionStorage instead.

api.explanation: Same idea as useLocalStorage, but persists in sessionStorage so the value survives refresh and is cleared when the tab closes.

arguments.name: key
arguments.description: sessionStorage key. Changing it re-reads that entry.

arguments.name: initialValue
arguments.description: Used when the key is missing or stored JSON cannot be parsed.

returns.description: A state tuple. setValue accepts a value or a function of the previous value, like useState.

fields.name: value
fields.description: Current parsed value.

fields.name: setValue
fields.description: Writes to React state and sessionStorage.

caveats: Values must be JSON-serializable.
Corrupt JSON in storage falls back to initialValue.
Write failures (quota, private mode) are ignored; state still updates in memory.

hooks.name: useOnlineStatus
hooks.summary: Subscribe to the browser online/offline state.
hooks.whenToUse: Use to warn users when the network drops.
hooks.description: You want to warn “you are offline” or disable Save when the laptop loses the network. This hook is the browser’s online flag, updated when the browser fires online and offline. It is not a ping of your API.

api.explanation: Subscribes to the browser online and offline events and returns whether the machine currently reports a network connection.

returns.description: true when the browser thinks it is online, false when it fires the offline event.

caveats: This is the browser’s connectivity flag, not a guarantee that your API is reachable.

hooks.name: useOnlineQueue
hooks.summary: Queue work while offline and flush when online.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for an in-memory outbox, not durable sync.
hooks.description: The user queued a comment on the train. Hold items in memory while navigator.onLine is false, then drain FIFO when the browser fires online. If processItem throws, that item stays at the front.

api.explanation: Queue values while the browser is offline. When online, items drain FIFO through processItem. If processItem throws, the failed item stays at the front.

arguments.name: processItem
arguments.description: Called for each queued item when the browser reports online.

returns.type: { enqueue, items, isOnline, isFlushing, error, flush }
returns.description: In-memory queue plus flush controls. Not persisted across refresh.

hooks.name: useStorageQuota
hooks.summary: Origin storage usage and quota from estimate().
hooks.whenToUse: Use to warn before the origin is out of space.
hooks.description: A PWA or editor writes large files and you need to warn before the origin quota is full. navigator.storage.estimate() after mount, with nulls when the API is missing.

api.explanation: Reads navigator.storage.estimate() after mount. Safe when the API is missing (SSR, older browsers).

returns.description: Bytes used and allowed, or nulls when unsupported.

fields.name: usage
fields.description: Bytes used.

fields.name: quota
fields.description: Bytes allowed.

fields.name: usageRatio
fields.description: usage / quota, or null.

fields.name: isSupported
fields.description: Whether estimate() exists.

fields.name: refresh
fields.description: Read estimate again.

hooks.name: useInstallPrompt
hooks.summary: Capture and replay the PWA beforeinstallprompt event.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for a custom Install button on Chromium.
hooks.description: Chromium fires beforeinstallprompt once. You must preventDefault to show your own Install button later. The hook holds that event, calls prompt(), and tracks standalone / appinstalled.

api.explanation: Captures beforeinstallprompt (Chromium), lets you call prompt() later, and tracks appinstalled / display-mode standalone.

returns.description: PWA install prompt state.

fields.name: isReady
fields.description: A deferred prompt is available.

fields.name: isInstalled
fields.description: Standalone display or appinstalled fired.

fields.name: prompt
fields.description: Shows the native install UI when ready.

caveats: Safari and Firefox do not fire beforeinstallprompt. isReady stays false there.

hooks.name: useCrossTabState
hooks.summary: JSON state synced across browser tabs.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for theme and flags that must match in every tab.
hooks.description: Theme, a draft flag, or a dismissed banner should match in every tab. Write JSON to localStorage and notify others through BroadcastChannel and the storage event. SSR returns the initial value.

api.explanation: useState that writes JSON to localStorage and syncs other tabs via BroadcastChannel and the storage event. Same tab already has the new value from the setter.

arguments.name: key
arguments.description: localStorage key.

arguments.name: initialValue
arguments.description: Used when the key is empty or JSON is invalid.

returns.description: Tuple like useState, including functional updates.

hooks.name: useFingerprint
hooks.summary: Client-side visitor id from browser fingerprint signals.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for anonymous visitor hints without cookies or a backend.
hooks.description: You need a stable-enough visitor id in the browser without cookies or a backend — for abuse hints, anonymous personalization, or correlating sessions. The hook samples canvas, WebGL, screen, locale, and related signals, hashes them client-side, and exposes refresh(). No API key and no network call (unlike Fingerprint’s commercial Identification product).

api.explanation: Collects browser signals (user agent, canvas, WebGL, screen, locale, storage) and hashes them into a stable client-side visitor id — similar to the open-source FingerprintJS approach. No network calls and no API key.

arguments.name: options.enabled
arguments.description: When false, skip automatic identification on mount. Call refresh() yourself. Default true.

returns.description: Visitor id plus the raw signal map used to build it.

fields.name: visitorId
fields.description: Hex hash of the collected signals, or null before the first successful run.

fields.name: components
fields.description: Named browser signals that went into the hash.

fields.name: isPending
fields.description: true while identification is running.

fields.name: error
fields.description: Set when collection throws unexpectedly.

fields.name: refresh
fields.description: Re-run identification and return the new visitor id.

caveats: This is client-side fingerprinting only. Identical devices can share an id; it is not Fingerprint Identification (the commercial SaaS).
Privacy-focused browsers may reduce signal entropy. Treat the id as a hint, not a hard identity.

hooks.name: useMediaQuery
hooks.summary: Subscribe to a CSS media query.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for layout branches that match CSS breakpoints.
hooks.description: Layout should change at the same breakpoint as CSS, for example a compact toolbar under 768px. Match the query in JS without resize listeners and leftover subscriptions.

api.explanation: Subscribes to window.matchMedia so your component re-renders when the query starts or stops matching, the same way CSS breakpoints work.

arguments.name: query
arguments.description: A CSS media query, for example "(min-width: 768px)" or "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)".

returns.description: true while the query matches the current viewport / environment.

hooks.name: useWindowSize
hooks.summary: Current viewport width and height.
hooks.whenToUse: Use when you need pixel dimensions, not just a breakpoint.
hooks.description: You need the actual pixel width or height: a canvas, a chart, a split pane. A media query is not enough. This hook tracks innerWidth and innerHeight on resize.

api.explanation: Tracks window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight and updates on resize. Use this when you need pixel sizes, not just a breakpoint.

returns.description: Viewport dimensions in CSS pixels.

fields.name: width
fields.description: window.innerWidth

fields.name: height
fields.description: window.innerHeight

hooks.name: useOnClickOutside
hooks.summary: Run a handler when the user clicks outside a ref.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for popovers, dropdowns, and dismissible cards.
hooks.description: A popover or dropdown should close when the user presses outside it. Attach a ref to the surface and pass a close handler. Inside clicks stay ignored.

api.explanation: Listens for mousedown and touchstart on the document. If the event target is outside ref.current, it calls handler. Use this to dismiss popovers.

arguments.name: ref
arguments.description: Ref attached to the element that should count as “inside”.

arguments.name: handler
arguments.description: Called only for presses that happen outside that element.

returns.description: Nothing. Typically you close local state from handler.

hooks.name: useOverlay
hooks.summary: Promise-based overlay / modal rendering.
hooks.whenToUse: Use when a modal should await the user’s choice.
hooks.description: You need a modal that the caller can await, like window.confirm but with your own UI. open(props) returns a promise; close(result) resolves it. Use it for delete confirms, pickers, and any dialog that must return a value before the flow continues.

api.explanation: Turns a modal component into a promise. You call open(props), the overlay renders, and close(result) resolves that promise. Body scroll is locked while it is open.

arguments.name: Overlay
arguments.description: Your UI. It receives the props you pass to open(), plus isOpen and close. Keep showing it when isOpen is false if you need an exit animation.

returns.description: Control the overlay from the parent and place it in the tree with render().

fields.name: open
fields.description: Shows the overlay and waits until close is called.

fields.name: close
fields.description: Hides the overlay, restores overflow, and resolves the pending open() promise.

fields.name: render
fields.description: Returns the overlay element, or null before the first open(). Put this in JSX.

caveats: render() is null until open() has been called once.
close() without a matching open() is a no-op for the promise.

hooks.name: useStepFlow
hooks.summary: Multi-step wizard that resolves when the flow finishes.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for onboarding or checkout-style sequences.
hooks.description: Onboarding, checkout, or a three-screen import wizard. Each step is a component. next() starts the flow and resolves with every step’s data when the last step finishes, or null if the user cancels.

api.explanation: Runs an ordered list of step components. next() starts the wizard and returns a promise for every step’s data. The last onNext resolves that promise; cancel resolves null.

arguments.name: steps
arguments.description: Components rendered one at a time. Each receives stepIndex, isLastStep, onNext, and onCancel.

returns.type: { next, cancel, completeStep, renderCurrentStep, currentStepIndex, isActive }
returns.description: Start/stop the flow and render the active step.

fields.name: next
fields.description: Starts from step 0. Resolves with collected step data, or null on cancel.

fields.name: cancel
fields.description: Aborts, resets the index, resolves next() with null.

fields.name: completeStep
fields.description: Records data and advances. Same function passed to each step as onNext.

fields.name: renderCurrentStep
fields.description: The active step, or null when the flow is inactive. extraProps are spread onto the step.

fields.name: currentStepIndex
fields.description: Zero-based index of the visible step.

fields.name: isActive
fields.description: True between next() and finish/cancel.

hooks.name: useAsyncSelect
hooks.summary: Open the native file picker and await the result.
hooks.whenToUse: Use instead of a hidden file input when you want a Promise.
hooks.description: A button should open the native file picker and you want a Promise, not a hidden <input type="file"> in JSX. Call the function from a click, await the File (or File[]), and get null if they cancel.

api.explanation: Returns a function that opens the native file picker and resolves with the chosen file(s). There is no visible input in your tree; the hook creates a temporary one.

returns.description: Call this from a click handler. Await the picker result.

fields.name: options.accept
fields.description: Same as the input accept attribute, e.g. "image/*" or ".pdf".

fields.name: options.multiple
fields.description: When true, the promise resolves to File[]. When false, it resolves to a single File.

caveats: Resolves null if the user cancels the picker or selects nothing.
Must be triggered from a user gesture (click) or the browser may block the picker.

hooks.name: useEventListener
hooks.summary: Subscribe to a DOM or window event with a stable handler.
hooks.whenToUse: Use instead of addEventListener in an effect you would rewrite often.
hooks.description: You need a resize, keydown, or custom event on window, document, or a node, without re-binding every render. Pass the target, type, and handler. The hook keeps the latest handler and cleans up on unmount.

api.explanation: Adds an event listener on a window, document, node, or ref. The handler ref stays current so the subscription does not reset every render.

arguments.name: target
arguments.type: Window | Document | EventTarget | RefObject<EventTarget | null> | null
arguments.description: Where to listen. Pass null to skip attaching (SSR-safe).

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: Event name, for example "resize" or "keydown".

arguments.name: handler
arguments.description: Called for each matching event. Latest function is used.

arguments.name: options
arguments.description: Passed through to addEventListener.

returns.description: Nothing. Side effect only.

hooks.name: useTimeout
hooks.summary: Run a callback once after a delay. null pauses.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for one-shot delays, not repeating ticks (see useInterval).
hooks.description: Run something once after a delay: a splash screen, a deferred toast. Pass null to cancel. Unlike useInterval, this fires once.

api.explanation: Runs callback once after delayMs. Pass null to pause or clear. The latest callback is used without restarting the timer.

arguments.name: callback
arguments.description: Invoked once when the timer fires.

arguments.name: delayMs
arguments.description: Delay in milliseconds. null means do not schedule.

returns.description: Nothing. Side effect only.

hooks.name: useKeyPress
hooks.summary: True while a keyboard key is held (ignores text fields).
hooks.whenToUse: Use for shortcuts such as Escape.
hooks.description: A shortcut such as Escape should flip a boolean while the key is held. Typing in inputs does not count.

api.explanation: True while that event.key is held down on window. Keydowns from inputs, textareas, selects, and contenteditable are ignored.

arguments.name: key
arguments.description: KeyboardEvent.key value, for example "Escape" or "k".

returns.description: true between matching keydown and keyup.

hooks.name: useScrollLock
hooks.summary: Lock and unlock document body scroll.
hooks.whenToUse: Use under modals and drawers so the page behind does not scroll.
hooks.description: A modal or drawer is open and the page behind should not scroll. Lock overflow on document.body, optionally pad for the scrollbar gutter, and unlock when the overlay closes.

api.explanation: Locks scrolling on document.body (overflow hidden, optional scrollbar gutter padding). Useful under modals and drawers so the page behind does not scroll.

arguments.name: options.autoLock
arguments.description: When true, locks on mount and unlocks on unmount.

arguments.name: options.widthReflow
arguments.description: When true, pads the body to compensate for the missing scrollbar width.

returns.description: Lock state plus imperative controls.

fields.name: isLocked
fields.description: Whether body scroll is currently locked.

fields.name: lock
fields.description: Locks body scroll.

fields.name: unlock
fields.description: Restores previous overflow and padding.

caveats: No-op during SSR. Pair autoLock with a modal open flag when needed.

hooks.name: useDocumentVisibility
hooks.summary: Whether the document tab is visible or hidden.
hooks.whenToUse: Use to pause polling or media when the tab is in the background.
hooks.description: The tab is hidden and you should pause polling, video, or expensive work. This is document.visibilityState as a React value — visible or hidden.

api.explanation: Subscribes to the Page Visibility API and returns whether the document is visible or hidden. Use it to pause polling or media when the tab is in the background.

returns.description: Current document.visibilityState. SSR defaults to visible.

hooks.name: useIdle
hooks.summary: True after a period of no user activity.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for soft session timeouts and away indicators.
hooks.description: You need a soft “away” or session-timeout signal. After a quiet period with no mouse, keyboard, touch, or scroll, the hook reports idle until the user moves again.

api.explanation: Returns true after timeoutMs of no pointer, keyboard, touch, or scroll activity. Useful for soft session timeouts and “away” UI.

arguments.name: timeoutMs
arguments.description: Idle threshold in milliseconds.

returns.description: true once the user has been inactive for timeoutMs.

hooks.name: useKeyboardShortcut
hooks.summary: Register a key combo on window and clean it up.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for command palette and Escape, not key-held state.
hooks.description: Command/Ctrl+K, Escape, or Shift+? should run a handler and unregister on unmount. Combos are plus-separated. Typing in inputs is ignored unless you turn that off.

api.explanation: Listens on window keydown for a combo such as ctrl+k, meta+s, or Escape. Cleans up on unmount. By default ignores typing in inputs and calls preventDefault.

arguments.name: shortcut
arguments.description: Plus-separated combo. Use mod for Command on Apple and Control elsewhere.

arguments.name: handler
arguments.description: Called when the combo matches.

arguments.name: options.ignoreInputs
arguments.description: Skip INPUT, TEXTAREA, SELECT, and contenteditable. Default true.

arguments.name: options.enabled
arguments.description: Detach the listener when false. Default true.

returns.description: No return value. The listener is registered for the lifetime of the component.

hooks.name: useLongPress
hooks.summary: Mouse and touch press-and-hold handlers.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for context menus on cards and list rows.
hooks.description: A card or list row should open a menu on press-and-hold, on mouse and touch. Moving past a pixel threshold or releasing early cancels. Spread the returned handlers onto the element.

api.explanation: Returns mouse and touch handlers. After delayMs without moving past moveThresholdPx, onLongPress fires. Spread the handlers onto the target element.

arguments.name: onLongPress
arguments.description: Called once the press is held long enough.

arguments.name: options.delayMs
arguments.description: Hold time. Default 500.

arguments.name: options.moveThresholdPx
arguments.description: Cancel if the pointer moves this far. Default 10.

returns.type: { onMouseDown, onMouseUp, onMouseLeave, onMouseMove, onTouchStart, onTouchEnd, onTouchMove, onContextMenu }
returns.description: Spread onto a button or surface.

hooks.name: useStableCallback
hooks.summary: Stable function identity, always-latest implementation.
hooks.whenToUse: Use in intervals, subscriptions, and memoized children.
hooks.description: You pass a callback into an interval, a subscription, or a child that memoizes on function identity. If you put the function in the dependency array, the subscription resets; if you omit it, you capture stale state. useStableCallback is one function identity that always calls the latest code.

api.explanation: Returns a function with a stable identity that always calls the latest fn you passed. Use it when a subscription or interval should not reset, but should see fresh state.

arguments.name: fn
arguments.description: The function you would normally recreate every render.

returns.description: A stable callback. Put this in dependency arrays; it will not change.

hooks.name: useUpdateEffect
hooks.summary: useEffect that skips the first mount.
hooks.whenToUse: Use when a side effect should run only after deps change, not on first paint.
hooks.description: You need a useEffect that should not fire on first paint — only when state, props, or context values change later. Same cleanup rules as useEffect. Put the values that matter in the dependency array.

api.explanation: Same as useEffect, but skips the first mount. The effect runs only when dependencies change afterward — state, props, or context values you list in deps. Cleanup still runs between updates and on unmount.

arguments.name: effect
arguments.description: Setup function. May return a cleanup function, like useEffect.

arguments.name: deps
arguments.description: Dependency list. Put the state, props, or context values that should trigger the effect.

returns.description: Nothing. Drive side effects from the effect body.

caveats: With deps [] the effect never runs: mount is skipped and nothing changes later.
Omitting deps re-runs after every render (after the first), same caveat as useEffect.

hooks.name: useResetState
hooks.summary: Local state that resets when the source key changes.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for drafts keyed by user id or record id.
hooks.description: You edit a draft for user A, then the route changes to user B. Local state still shows A’s name because you synced with useEffect and missed a dependency. useResetState takes a source key (the user id). When the key changes, state is the new initial value. Same idea as key={userId} on a form, as a hook.

api.explanation: Like useState(initialValue), but when source changes (user id, record id, open flag), state becomes the initialValue from that render.

arguments.name: source
arguments.description: Identity of the thing being edited. Changing it resets state.

arguments.name: initialValue
arguments.description: State to use on first render and whenever source changes.

returns.description: The same tuple shape as useState.

fields.name: state
fields.description: Current local value.

fields.name: setState
fields.description: Update state until source changes.

hooks.name: useAsyncAction
hooks.summary: Pending, error, and data around one async action.
hooks.whenToUse: Use on Save/Send buttons, not for list fetching.
hooks.description: A Save, Send, or “Generate report” button. You need pending, error, and the last result, and you must ignore a response if the user fired the action again. This is not a query cache. It is the mutation UI around one async function.

api.explanation: Wraps one async function for button UIs: pending, last data, last error, and run(). A newer run ignores an older result. This is not a shared cache.

arguments.name: action
arguments.description: The work to run. The hook always calls the latest version.

returns.description: Call run from a click handler. Disable the button with isPending.

fields.name: run
fields.description: Starts the action. Re-throws if action throws.

fields.name: isPending
fields.description: True while the latest run is in flight.

fields.name: error
fields.description: Rejection from the latest finished run, or null.

fields.name: data
fields.description: Resolution from the latest successful run.

fields.name: reset
fields.description: Clears pending, error, and data and invalidates in-flight runs.

hooks.name: useAsyncState
hooks.summary: Typed idle, loading, success, and error for async work.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for fetches with abort, not for a shared query cache.
hooks.description: A load that has idle, loading, success, and error — and a second request must not overwrite the first after it finishes late. execute() aborts the previous run. immediate plus source refetch when an id changes. Honor AbortSignal in fetch.

api.explanation: Typed idle / loading / success / error around an async function. A newer execute aborts the previous run. Pass immediate to fetch on mount, and source to refetch when a key changes.

arguments.name: fn
arguments.description: The work to run. Honor signal.aborted when you can.

arguments.name: options.immediate
arguments.description: Run once on mount (and when source changes). Default false.

arguments.name: options.source
arguments.description: When this value changes and immediate is true, execute again.

returns.type: { status, data, error, isIdle, isLoading, isSuccess, isError, execute, abort, reset }
returns.description: Discriminated-style status flags plus controls.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Current phase.

fields.name: execute
fields.description: Starts a new run and aborts the previous one.

fields.name: abort
fields.description: Aborts the in-flight run without resetting data.

fields.name: reset
fields.description: Aborts and returns to idle.

hooks.name: useOptimisticAction
hooks.summary: Apply a local update, confirm or roll back.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for likes and steppers that must feel instant.
hooks.description: A like, follow, or stepper should move immediately, then wait for the server. If the request fails, the old value must come back. Duplicate clicks while pending are ignored.

api.explanation: Applies optimistic() immediately, then awaits action(). On success the confirmed value replaces it. On failure the previous value is restored. A second run while pending is ignored.

arguments.name: initialValue
arguments.description: Starting value.

arguments.name: action
arguments.description: Server or async confirmation. Receives the optimistic value.

arguments.name: optimistic
arguments.description: Synchronous next value shown before action resolves.

returns.description: Optimistic state and a run() that rolls back on failure.

hooks.name: useRetry
hooks.summary: Retry an async function with backoff and cancel.
hooks.whenToUse: Use when a single call may fail transiently.
hooks.description: The network blipped. You want N extra attempts, exponential backoff, and a way to cancel waiting between tries. This is the loop around one async function, not a query cache.

api.explanation: Calls fn and retries on failure with constant or exponential backoff. cancel() aborts waiting between attempts.

arguments.name: fn
arguments.description: The work to retry.

arguments.name: options.retries
arguments.description: Extra attempts after the first. Default 3.

arguments.name: options.delayMs
arguments.description: Base delay between attempts. Default 250.

arguments.name: options.backoff
arguments.description: Default exponential.

returns.description: run() starts the loop. cancel() stops further retries.

hooks.name: useAsyncQueue
hooks.summary: FIFO async tasks with a concurrency cap.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for uploads and sequential outbound work.
hooks.description: Uploads, outbound messages, or “process these one or two at a time.” enqueue() returns a promise; concurrency caps how many run; clear() drops work still waiting.

api.explanation: FIFO queue of async tasks with a concurrency cap. enqueue() returns the task promise. clear() rejects work still waiting, not work already running.

arguments.name: options.concurrency
arguments.description: How many tasks may run at once. Default 1.

returns.description: Queue controls.

fields.name: enqueue
fields.description: Adds work and starts it when a slot is free.

fields.name: size
fields.description: Tasks waiting.

fields.name: pending
fields.description: Tasks running.

fields.name: clear
fields.description: Reject waiting tasks with AbortError.

hooks.name: usePolling
hooks.summary: Interval polling that pauses when the tab is hidden.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for unread badges and live boards.
hooks.description: Refresh unread counts or a live board on an interval. Pause when the tab is hidden, abort the in-flight tick on unmount, and pass null to stop without tearing the component down.

api.explanation: Calls fn on an interval. Pass null to pause. By default polling stops while the tab is hidden and the previous tick is aborted when a new one starts or the effect cleans up.

arguments.name: fn
arguments.description: Work for each tick.

arguments.name: intervalMs
arguments.description: Delay between ticks, or null to pause.

arguments.name: options.pauseWhenHidden
arguments.description: Pause when document.visibilityState is hidden. Default true.

arguments.name: options.immediate
arguments.description: Run once immediately. Default true.

returns.description: Whether the interval is active, and the last tick error.

hooks.name: useRenderTracker
hooks.summary: Count renders and log commits in development.
hooks.whenToUse: Use to spot unexpected rerenders. Disable in production.
hooks.description: A child re-renders more than you expect. The hook counts function invocations and, in development, logs after commit. Disable in production with the default NODE_ENV check or enabled: false.

api.explanation: Increments a render counter each time the component function runs. In development it logs after commit. Pass enabled: false (or rely on production NODE_ENV) to skip logging.

arguments.name: label
arguments.description: Name printed in the console.

arguments.name: options.enabled
arguments.description: Default: process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production".

returns.description: How many times this hook instance has rendered.

hooks.name: useWhyDidYouUpdate
hooks.summary: Log which values changed between renders.
hooks.whenToUse: Use in development when a memoized child still updates.
hooks.description: You know it re-rendered; you need which prop or value changed. Pass a snapshot object. Development logs keys that failed Object.is. No-op logging when disabled.

api.explanation: Compares the props object to the previous render and logs keys whose values changed by Object.is. Disabled in production unless you pass enabled: true.

arguments.name: label
arguments.description: Name printed in the console.

arguments.name: props
arguments.description: Values to diff, usually props or a state snapshot.

arguments.name: options.enabled
arguments.description: Default: process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production".

returns.description: No return value. Output goes to console.debug.

hooks.name: useDebouncedCallback
hooks.summary: Debounce calling a function, with cancel.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for search fetch and persist-on-type.
hooks.description: You want to debounce work, not a displayed value: search fetch, persist on type, resize handler. useDebounce lags a value for rendering. useDebouncedCallback lags calling a function and can cancel the pending call.

api.explanation: Returns a function that waits delayMs after the last call before running callback. Also returns cancel to drop a pending call.

arguments.name: callback
arguments.description: The work to run after idle time. Latest callback is used.

arguments.name: delayMs
arguments.description: Idle time in milliseconds.

returns.description: A tuple: the debounced function and a cancel function.

fields.name: run
fields.description: Call this from events. Restarts the timer each time.

fields.name: cancel
fields.description: Clears the timer so callback will not run.

hooks.name: useThrottledCallback
hooks.summary: Throttle calling a function, with cancel.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for scroll, resize, and rapid search fetch.
hooks.description: You want to throttle work, not a displayed value: scroll handlers, resize listeners, rapid search. Leading call runs immediately; a trailing call keeps the latest args. cancel drops a pending trailing run.

api.explanation: Returns a function that invokes callback at most once per delayMs (leading + trailing). Also returns cancel to drop a pending trailing call.

arguments.name: callback
arguments.description: The work to run. Latest callback is used.

arguments.name: delayMs
arguments.description: Minimum milliseconds between invocations.

returns.description: A tuple: the throttled function and a cancel function.

fields.name: run
fields.description: Call this from events. Leading call runs immediately when the window is open.

fields.name: cancel
fields.description: Clears a pending trailing call.

hooks.name: useFields
hooks.summary: Small form state with setField, dirty, and optional schema.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for modals and settings, not huge RHF forms.
hooks.description: A modal or settings card with five fields. You do not want React Hook Form for that, and you do not want useState per input. One object, setField, dirty flag, optional schema (Zod-shaped safeParse), and submit(onValid).

api.explanation: One object of form values with setField, dirty tracking, and optional schema.safeParse (Zod-compatible). submit(onValid) only runs onValid when parse succeeds.

arguments.name: initialValues
arguments.description: Starting values. Keep this object stable or isDirty will flicker.

arguments.name: schema
arguments.type: { safeParse(data) => { success, data } | { success: false, error: { issues } } }
arguments.description: Zod schemas work. Issues use path[0] as the field name.

returns.type: { values, setField, setValues, reset, isDirty, errors, validate, submit }
returns.description: Bind inputs to values and setField. Show errors[field] under the input.

fields.name: values
fields.description: Current field values.

fields.name: setField
fields.description: Updates one key and clears that key’s error.

fields.name: setValues
fields.description: Replace or functional-update the whole object.

fields.name: reset
fields.description: Back to initialValues, no errors.

fields.name: isDirty
fields.description: True when any value differs (shallow) from initialValues.

fields.name: errors
fields.description: First message per field from the last validate/submit.

fields.name: validate
fields.description: Runs schema if present.

fields.name: submit
fields.description: Validates, then calls onValid(values) only when ok.

hooks.name: useAmountInput
hooks.summary: Locale amount input with grouping, decimals, and cursor restore.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for price and invoice fields, not generic text.
hooks.description: A price, invoice, or quantity field that must look local while you type: French spaces, Dutch dots, English commas, and a cursor that does not jump when grouping appears. The input shows the formatted string; submit still gets a canonical "12345.67". Pass language, decimalCount, and the returned ref. Add locales to register or override languages beyond en/de/nl/fr.

api.explanation: Formats a money-like input as the user types: thousand separators, locale decimal, and a stable cursor. Bind displayValue, onChange, onBlur, and ref to the input. value is the canonical string for submit (dot decimal, no grouping).

arguments.name: language
arguments.description: Picks grouping and decimal characters. Built-ins: en 1,234.56; fr/de 1 234,56; nl 1.234,56. Custom codes need an entry in locales.

arguments.name: decimalCount
arguments.description: Maximum digits after the decimal. Extra fractional digits are dropped.

arguments.name: defaultValue
arguments.description: Starting canonical amount. reset() returns here.

arguments.name: locales
arguments.description: Optional map of extra or override locale configs. Unknown languages and invalid configs (same separators) fall back to en.

returns.type: { value, displayValue, onChange, onBlur, ref, reset, updateValue }
returns.description: Pass displayValue and the handlers to the input. Read value when you persist.

fields.name: value
fields.description: Unformatted canonical amount, e.g. "12345.67". Empty string when blank.

fields.name: displayValue
fields.description: Formatted text for the input, e.g. "12 345,67".

fields.name: onChange
fields.description: Normalizes, formats, and restores the cursor after grouping changes.

fields.name: onBlur
fields.description: Re-normalizes the current display on blur.

fields.name: ref
fields.description: Required so the hook can restore selection after format.

fields.name: reset
fields.description: Restores defaultValue.

fields.name: updateValue
fields.description: Set from outside (number, string, null). Replaces the field.

caveats: Attach the returned ref. Cursor restoration reads the live input node.
value is not what you put in the input. Bind displayValue.
Changing language or decimalCount does not rewrite an in-progress value; remount or call updateValue.

hooks.name: useList
hooks.summary: Insert, update, remove, and reorder items with ids.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for todos, attendees, and pipeline stages.
hooks.description: A list the user can add to, rename, delete, and reorder: todos, attendees, stages. Instead of spreading arrays in every handler, you get insert, update, remove, and move on items that have an id.

api.explanation: Holds an array of items with id and exposes insert, update, remove, move, and replace so list screens do not hand-spread arrays.

arguments.name: initialItems
arguments.description: Starting list. Each item must have a string id.

returns.type: { items, insert, update, remove, move, replace, setItems }
returns.description: The list and the mutations.

fields.name: items
fields.description: Current array.

fields.name: insert
fields.description: Appends, or inserts at index.

fields.name: update
fields.description: Merges a partial or maps one item.

fields.name: remove
fields.description: Drops the item with that id.

fields.name: move
fields.description: Reorders one item. No-op if indexes are out of range.

fields.name: replace
fields.description: Swap the whole list (for example after fetch).

hooks.name: useSelection
hooks.summary: Single or multi id selection for lists and tables.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for checkboxes and “select all on this page”.
hooks.description: A table or checklist: click to select, cmd-click to multi-select, “select all on this page,” clear. You should not keep a Set in three places. useSelection is the selected ids and those operations, single or multiple.

api.explanation: Selected ids for a list or table. multiple (default) toggles membership; single keeps at most one id.

arguments.name: mode
arguments.description: Whether more than one id can be selected.

arguments.name: initial
arguments.description: Ids selected on first render.

returns.type: { selected, isSelected, toggle, selectOnly, selectAll, clear, setSelected }
returns.description: selected is a string[] in click order.

fields.name: selected
fields.description: Currently selected ids.

fields.name: isSelected
fields.description: Whether id is in the selection.

fields.name: toggle
fields.description: Add/remove in multiple; replace or clear in single.

fields.name: selectOnly
fields.description: Selection becomes exactly this id.

fields.name: selectAll
fields.description: Select these ids (first only in single mode).

fields.name: clear
fields.description: Empty selection.

hooks.name: useSearchState
hooks.summary: URL search params as React state.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for filters, tabs, and page that must be shareable.
hooks.description: Filters, tabs, and page number should live in the URL so refresh and share work. People sync useState to search params with useEffect and fight loops. This hook is the query string as state: read it, set it, the address bar updates.

api.explanation: Treat location.search as state. Keys come from defaults (all strings). Empty strings are omitted from the URL. Updates use history.replaceState so the back button is not flooded.

arguments.name: defaults
arguments.description: Default query values. Keep this object stable (module scope or useMemo).

returns.description: Like useState. setValues accepts a partial or a functional update.

fields.name: values
fields.description: Current params merged on top of defaults.

fields.name: setValues
fields.description: Writes the query string and notifies subscribers.

caveats: Hash routes still work; only location.search is read and written.

hooks.name: useConfirm
hooks.summary: Await a yes/no dialog from a click handler.
hooks.whenToUse: Use before delete or other destructive actions.
hooks.description: You need “Are you sure?” before delete, and you want to await the answer in the click handler. Same idea as useOverlay, with a default dialog. Call confirm({ title, danger }), put render() in the tree, branch on true/false.

api.explanation: Promise-based confirm dialog with a default UI. confirm(options) resolves true or false. You must render {render()} once in the tree.

returns.description: Same pattern as useOverlay, with a built-in dialog.

fields.name: confirm
fields.description: options: title, message?, confirmLabel?, cancelLabel?, danger?.

fields.name: render
fields.description: Place this in JSX. Null until the first confirm().

hooks.name: usePrompt
hooks.summary: Await a single string from a small dialog.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for rename and “name this view”.
hooks.description: You need a single string from the user — rename, “name this view” — without standing up a form page. await prompt({ title, label }) returns the string or null if they cancel. Render the dialog with render().

api.explanation: Promise-based prompt for a single string. prompt(options) resolves the string or null on cancel. Render {render()} in the tree.

returns.description: Built-in labeled input dialog.

fields.name: prompt
fields.description: options: title, message?, label?, initialValue?, confirmLabel?, cancelLabel?.

fields.name: render
fields.description: Place this in JSX.

hooks.name: useControllableState
hooks.summary: Controlled and uncontrolled state in one setter.
hooks.whenToUse: Use in reusable inputs, drawers, and tabs.
hooks.description: You are building a Switch, Tabs, or Drawer that must work in two ways: the parent owns the value, or the component owns it. Teams copy this if (value !== undefined) branch into every primitive. useControllableState is that branch: pass value to control it, omit value to stay uncontrolled, onChange always fires.

api.explanation: One setter for both controlled and uncontrolled components. If value is passed, the hook is controlled and only calls onChange. Otherwise it keeps defaultValue internally.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: Controlled value. Omit this to run uncontrolled.

arguments.name: defaultValue
arguments.description: Starting value when value is omitted.

arguments.name: onChange
arguments.description: Fires with the next value in both modes.

returns.description: Same shape as useState. setValue accepts a value or a functional update.

hooks.name: useUnsavedChanges
hooks.summary: Warn on tab close and confirm in-app leave when dirty.
hooks.whenToUse: Use on editors and long forms.
hooks.description: The user edited a form and hits Back, a sidebar link, or closes the tab. You need a beforeunload warning for the tab, and an awaitable confirm for in-app navigation. Wire isDirty from useFields or your form library, inject useConfirm if you want your own dialog, and call confirmLeave() before changing the route.

api.explanation: While isDirty is true, the tab’s beforeunload prompt is armed. confirmLeave() is for in-app navigation: it returns true if leaving is allowed.

arguments.name: isDirty
arguments.description: Whether there are unsaved edits.

arguments.name: confirmLeave
arguments.description: Injected confirmer (for example useConfirm). Falls back to window.confirm.

returns.description: Call before changing route. Resolves true when clean, or when the user agrees to leave.

fields.name: confirmLeave
fields.description: Default message: “Leave without saving?”

hooks.name: useElementSize
hooks.summary: Live width and height of an element via ResizeObserver.
hooks.whenToUse: Use for charts, split panes, and autosize fields.
hooks.description: A chart, canvas, or virtual list must match the box it lives in — not the window. useWindowSize re-renders on every viewport resize and still does not know the column width. Attach the callback ref; width and height track that node through ResizeObserver.

api.explanation: Callback ref plus live contentRect width and height from ResizeObserver. Measure the element, not the window.

returns.description: Attach ref to the node you want to measure. Starts at 0×0 until it mounts.

fields.name: ref
fields.description: Callback ref for the observed element.

fields.name: width
fields.description: contentRect.width

fields.name: height
fields.description: contentRect.height

hooks.name: useInView
hooks.summary: Whether an element intersects the viewport (or a root).
hooks.whenToUse: Use for lazy load, infinite scroll, and enter animations.
hooks.description: You want to load a heavy widget, fetch the next page, or start an animation only when the user can see the element. IntersectionObserver is the right API; the hook is the ref plus isInView. Set once if you only care about the first time it appears.

api.explanation: Callback ref plus isInView from IntersectionObserver. Use for lazy media, infinite-scroll sentinels, and enter animations.

arguments.name: root
arguments.description: Scroll root. Default is the viewport.

arguments.name: rootMargin
arguments.description: Same as IntersectionObserver rootMargin.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: How much of the target must be visible.

arguments.name: once
arguments.description: If true, stays true after the first intersection and disconnects.

returns.description: Attach ref to the target. isInView updates as it enters and leaves (unless once).

hooks.name: usePagination
hooks.summary: Page, page size, offset, and next/prev with clamping.
hooks.whenToUse: Use to slice lists and tables.
hooks.description: A table or gallery has 200 rows and you show 20 at a time. You need page, how many pages, the slice offset, and disabled next/prev. When a filter shrinks the list, the current page must clamp instead of pointing at empty space. usePagination is that math.

api.explanation: 1-based page state with derived pageCount, offset, and next/prev. Clamps page when total shrinks. Changing page size returns to page 1.

arguments.name: total
arguments.description: Total item count.

arguments.name: pageSize
arguments.description: Items per page (initial).

arguments.name: initialPage
arguments.description: Starting page (1-based).

returns.type: { page, pageSize, total, pageCount, offset, canNext, canPrev, setPage, setPageSize, next, prev }
returns.description: Slice with items.slice(offset, offset + pageSize).

fields.name: page
fields.description: Current page, always between 1 and pageCount.

fields.name: offset
fields.description: (page - 1) * pageSize

fields.name: pageCount
fields.description: At least 1, even when total is 0.

fields.name: setPageSize
fields.description: Updates page size and resets to page 1.
